description_en: The temple of Lāṭīkoilī is located 3 km south-west of Birendranagar and 2 km north-west of the Kãkrevihāra Buddhist temple (SRK0020).The dimensions of the temple, from the back wall to the front pillars are: 650 x 390 cm, with an approximate height of 570 cm.Thesanctumitself has the following dimensions: 400 x 390 cm. The temple is oriented towards the south-east.The architecture of the monument is unique for the region. Access to thesanctumis preceded by a vestibule with a row of four stone pillars. Thesanctumis occupied by a large stoneśivaliṅga. The room is covered by a corbelled dome. (Pictures are not allowed inside the temple.) Lustral waters are evacuated outside the temple through an uncarvedpraṇālalocated on the northeastern wall.Above the door is a stone inscription recording the construction of the temple under the auspices of Pratāp Śāhī and his nephew Māna Śāhī, in ŚS 1504 (1582 CE). The inscription was consecrated by Ātmanātha and Laṁgarnātha, two Nātha yogis. Interestingly, the inscription was written by a certain Rāṃa Kṛiṣṇa from Benares (Naraharinath 1956 (VS 2013), 168-169, cited inShrestha 2009, 280). The date follows the division of the Dailekh territory in two principalities (c. 1550's CE). Both entities are ruled by kings from the Rāskoṭi lineage.The temple was renovated in VS 2040 (1984 CE), as is recorded on an inscription engraved in the cement of the southwestern pillar. This renovation consisted in a complete dismantlement of the temple and reconstruction with cement mortar. The four front pillars have also been replaced by new ones.In front of the temple is a stone sculpture of Śiva's bull Nandi. An inscription from VS 2042 (1986 CE) is running on three sides of the base of the sculpture.The monument is also mentioned inSharma 1972, 21, 25-26;Sharma 2012, 166-168 andAndolfatto 2019, 65, 89-90.
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number SRK0030_I_001 Sources Naraharinath, Yogi. (1956). Itihāsa Prakāśa 2.1, Mrigasthali: Itihasa-Prakasa-Mandala. Shrestha, Tek Bahadur. (2009). "Dullu-Dailekh as Independant Principalities", in Marie Lecomte-Tilouine (ed.), Bards and Mediums. History, Culture and Politics in the Central Himalayan Kingdoms (Almora Book Depot: Almora), pp. 277-292.

historical_events.event_description: A four line inscription indevanāgarīscript is inserted above the temple's door. It is inscribed on stone. Yogi Naraharinath first mentioned it in 1956 (Naraharinath 1956 (VS 2013), 168-169, cited inShrestha 2009, 80).The inscription records the construction of the temple under the auspices of Pratāpa Śāhī and his nephew Māna Śāhī, in ŚS 1504 (1582 CE). It was consecrated by Ātmanātha and Laṁgarnātha, two Nātha yogis. Interestingly, the inscription was written by a certain Rāma Kṛṣṇa from Benares (Shrestha 2009, 280).
The inscription is incised in the cement covering the pilaster at the southern corner of the monument. It records the renovation of the temple in VS 2040 (1984 CE).
An inscription of four lines runs on the northeastern, northwestern and southwestern sides of the base of the Nandī stone sculpture. It records the installation of the sculpture in VS 2042 (1986 CE).
